first_impression: Gorgeous deck, bold claims. Agent-written, so I want to see the repo, tests and benchmarks run myself.
confusing: Slide 9 title 'Same answers' vs top-left plot where passive collapse visibly diverges (RMS 0.195 m, ~0.5 s phase offset)
Slide 10 stacks 40x, 22x, 121x, 3.7x and 32.8x; three headline multipliers, unclear which is the claim
Slide 14 shows MacGym 21.9 m, text says 22.0 m, slide 7 says 21.5 m; too many near-identical distances
Slide 12 '18 checks' listed as a feature count, not coverage; no physics-correctness tests named beyond NaN check
doubts: 40x compares a planar 2D impulse solver with MuJoCo's general 3D soft-contact solver; not apples to apples
'Agents wrote most of the code' plus 8 commits in 4 hours: is the 2D physics actually understood and verified, or just generated
Warm-start contact fix and DC-motor curve: is the 'cheating' story a real discovery or standard RL exploit hygiene
jax-metal 'consider it dead' quote needs a source link; MJX on Mac CPU not benchmarked
Fresh install 87 s used warm pip cache and committed HEAD; not a stranger's experience
questions: Why compare to MuJoCo C rollout and not a vectorized numpy/torch-MPS or Brax-style baseline at equal physics fidelity?
Which tests would fail if the Metal kernel had a sign error in joint torque?
How much of the kernel codegen did you write vs review? Show me a bug you found in agent output.
Is the license, packaging and API stable enough that I could accept a PR today?
Why does the PPO update take 72% of time, and have you tried MLX compile to shrink it?

fixes.change: Retitle to an honest claim ('Analytic cases match to 0.01%; walker contact matches for 0.6-0.8 s') and add one plain-language line explaining the divergence in the zero-torque case
Lead with one number (22x at the 4,096 you train with) and move 40x/121x to a footnote; state planar-2D asymmetry next to the bar chart, not below
Show a test-list or coverage snippet and a link to CI; name one concrete bug the tests caught
Add the source URL for the jax-metal quote on-slide or in notes
Replace the QR with a readable short URL plus repo badge showing tests passing, so judges can verify while he is speaking

first_impression: Visually excellent, but it reads as engineering showcase; claims need controls, statistics and a clear research question.
confusing: No stated hypothesis or research question; the cheating finding is told as a story rather than a controlled result
Slide 8 ablation is two rows with no n or seeds; is 6.64 vs 2.74 m/s one run?
Slide 7 mixes 8 s replay distances and whole-episode chart distances (21.5 m vs ~55 m); footnote helps but is small
Slide 14 transfer: 21.9 vs 19.8 m headline vs 19.7 +/- 0.9 and 22.0 elsewhere; inconsistent reporting
Slide 6 'days of practice' is simulated robot time, which a layperson reads as training time
doubts: Sim-to-sim with the same MJCF-like robot shows little about physical transfer; MuJoCo is also a simulator with similar assumptions
Mass +20% gave 3/20 falls and 15.6 +/- 5.2 m: the claim 'transfers' is stronger than the data
Contact model diverges from MuJoCo after 0.6-0.8 s, yet 'same final pose' is cited as agreement; resting pose is a weak test
5 seeds, mean +/- SD with no confidence interval or baseline algorithm comparison
Foot-slip metric is self-defined; no literature grounding on exploit detection in RL
questions: What is your null hypothesis for the cheating ablation and how many seeds per condition?
What prior work (Brax, MJX, Isaac Gym, Genesis) did you read, and how does your contact model differ from theirs?
Why does your impulse solver diverge from MuJoCo in the passive collapse case; which model is closer to real physics?
Did you run the 40x benchmark with variance across repeated runs and thermal throttling controls?
What would falsify the claim that the torque-speed curve is the real fix?

fixes.change: Show the full ablation as a small table (baseline, warm-start only, motor curve only, both) with seeds per cell and mean +/- SD for speed and slip
Reconcile the headline numbers (one distance per condition, same n) and rename to 'Sim-to-sim robustness' while naming mass +20% as the failure case on the slide
Add a one-line explanation and a quantitative error table (RMS per scenario, 0.5 s window) rather than six unlabelled plots
State a research question in one sentence ('Can a laptop GPU match CPU sim fidelity for RL teaching at 20x+ throughput?')
Add error bars / run count to the 6.8M vs 165K bars and mention hardware, batch size and thermal state
